model_priors.model_reasoning: AXL is a well-characterized receptor tyrosine kinase (RTK) of the TAM family (TYRO3, AXL, MERTK). It is known to undergo robust ligand-induced (Gas6) internalization and degradation, as well as constitutive/basal internalization. The cytoplasmic tail is large (~422 aa) and contains the kinase domain plus multiple endocytic-relevant features. Inspection of the cytoplasmic region reveals a canonical NPXY motif (NPVY near the juxtamembrane region), tyrosine-based motifs, and the receptor undergoes ubiquitin-mediated lysosomal degradation after activation. Even basally, AXL shows constitutive turnover typical of RTKs. The protein is a well-known target for internalization-based therapeutic strategies precisely because of its high endocytic propensity. Only one isoform is provided here.

per_isoform.topology_summary: Signal peptide (1–32), extracellular domain (~419 aa), single TM helix, large cytoplasmic tail (~422 aa) containing the kinase domain and C-terminal regulatory region.
per_isoform.endocytic_motifs_noted: Cytoplasmic region contains: NPVY (NPXY-type motif, juxtamembrane region, supports clathrin-mediated endocytosis via PTB-domain adaptors); multiple tyrosine-based motifs (YXX[hydrophobic] candidates) within the kinase and C-terminal tail; ubiquitination sites supporting lysosomal routing; dileucine-like sequences in the C-terminal tail. Specific sequence scan of cytoplasmic region: '...NMSVCVADFGLSKKIYNGDYYRQGR...' and '...YLSTKRFIHRDLAARNCML...' contain YXX[hydrophobic] patterns. NPVY is present in the juxtamembrane segment.
per_isoform.rationale: AXL is a TAM-family RTK with well-documented rapid internalization and lysosomal degradation upon Gas6 binding, and measurable constitutive/basal turnover. The large cytoplasmic tail harbors an NPXY (NPVY) motif, multiple tyrosine-based sequences, and ubiquitination-competent lysines. Family-level knowledge strongly supports high intrinsic endocytic propensity. This is consistent with AXL's role in signal termination via receptor downregulation and its exploitation as an ADC/internalization target.

basal.rationale: No evidence in the ledger describes constitutive, ligand-independent AXL internalization.

native_ligand.rationale: GAS6-AXL signalling drives synaptic internalisation by AXL+ OPCs in early human brain development (int_evi_05), and pharmacological TAM receptor inhibition plus targeted AXL knockdown impairs synaptic uptake (int_evi_04), together demonstrating functional, ligand-driven AXL internalization. Additionally, SFTSV (acting via AXL as entry receptor) triggers AXL autophosphorylation and macropinocytotic internalization via PI3K/PLC (int_evi_01, int_evi_02), though this is a viral rather than canonical endogenous ligand context. Magnitude is graded moderate because no quantitative internalization rates are provided.

therapeutic.rationale: Anti-AXL monoclonal antibody mAb654 is suggested to exert anti-tumor effects partly through induction of AXL receptor endocytosis (int_evi_03), but this is described as a possible mechanism rather than directly measured internalization, and no quantitative data are provided.

literature.rationale: AXL shows consistent evidence of ligand-driven internalization across multiple contexts: GAS6-stimulated synaptic uptake in primary human OPCs and macropinocytotic entry triggered by viral engagement of AXL. Therapeutic antibody-induced endocytosis is suggested but not directly quantified. No basal internalization data are present. Overall, AXL is a moderately internalizing receptor with well-characterized ligand-driven endocytic activity.
literature.cross_condition_note: Ligand-driven AXL internalization occurs via macropinocytosis in the context of viral entry (SFTSV, PI3K/PLC-dependent) and via a GAS6-dependent pathway in primary human OPCs during brain development; therapeutic antibody-induced internalization is inferred rather than directly measured, making the native-ligand mode better supported than the therapeutic mode in this ledger.

sources.claim: AXL-mediated SFTSV infection proceeds via a macropinocytotic entry pathway, triggered by AXL autophosphorylation and recruitment of PI3K and PLC, characterizing the endocytic route used for AXL-dependent viral internalization.

source.title: SFTSV utilizes AXL/GAS6 for entry via PI3K-PLC-dependent macropinocytosis activated by AXL-kinase

spans.quote: This interaction induces autophosphorylation of tyrosine residues in the intracellular domain of AXL, recruiting phosphatidylinositol-3 kinase (PI3K) and phospholipase C (PLC) and establishing a macropinocytotic pathway of SFTSV entry.

sources.claim: AXL mediates SFTSV entry via a PI3K/PLC-dependent macropinocytosis pathway, establishing AXL's internalization route as macropinocytosis.

source.title: SFTSV utilizes AXL/GAS6 for entry via PI3K-PLC-dependent macropinocytosis activated by AXL-kinase

spans.quote: This study uncovered AXL as a potential entry receptor for SFTS virus (SFTSV) via PI3K/PLC-dependent macropinocytosis pathway distinct from previously reported viral entry mechanism.

sources.claim: An anti-AXL monoclonal antibody (mAb654) may exert superior anti-tumor effects partly through induction of AXL receptor endocytosis, suggesting antibody-induced AXL internalization as a mechanism of action.

cell_context.disease_state: EGFR-mutant lung cancer with osimertinib resistance

source.title: A bispecific antibody targeting EGFR and AXL delays resistance to osimertinib

spans.quote: While no pair of osimertinib and an anti-AXL drug is able to prevent relapses, triplets combining osimertinib, cetuximab (an anti-EGFR antibody), and either anti-AXL drug are initially effective. However, longer monitoring uncovers superiority of the mAb654-containing triplet, possibly due to induction of receptor endocytosis, activation of immune mechanisms, or disabling intrinsic mutators. Hence, we constructed a bispecific antibody that engages both AXL and EGFR. When combined with osimertinib, the bispecific antibody consistently inhibits tumor relapses, which warrants clinical trials.

sources.claim: Pharmacological inhibition of TAM receptors (including AXL) in a dose-dependent manner, and targeted reduction of AXL expression in OPCs, impairs synaptic uptake, demonstrating that AXL drives internalization of synaptic material by OPCs.

source.title: Human oligodendrocyte progenitor cells mediate synapse elimination through TAM receptor activation

spans.quote: Further, dose-dependent pharmacological inhibition of TAM receptors demonstrates the importance of AXL, and targeted reduction of AXL expression in OPCs impairs synaptic uptake.
